tagline.text: A Benguet ridge traverse linking pine and mossy forest

location.label: Location
location.text: Japas trailhead, Bokod, Benguet Province, to Ekip village

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: 2 days and 1 night (a day traverse is also possible)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) in Manila, then overland to Baguio

children.text: Starting from Bokod in Benguet, this roughly 26 km traverse links Mt. Pack, Mt. Purgatory, Bakian, Tangbao and Mt. Komkompol. It passes through pine forest and mossy forest, and a local Ibaloi guide is required.

The Mt. Purgatory Traverse is a long ridge trek in Bokod, in the northeast of Benguet. It lies in the mountain country between Mt. Pulag and Mt. Ugo, and locals also call this area Mangisi. The route starts at the Japas trailhead and ends at Ekip village, a one-way traverse whose total length is given as about
26km
to
30km
depending on the source. Japas is at the edge of Bobok-Bisal village and Ekip is a mountain village within the same municipality, so you see everyday highland life all along the way.

The route strings together six peaks and rest points: Mangangew, Mt. Pack, Mt. Purgatory, Bakian, Tangbao and Mt. Komkompol. Only three of them count as true summits; the others are viewpoints or campsites. The highest point is Mt. Komkompol at about
, with Mt. Pack at about
and Mt. Purgatory at about
. Elevations differ slightly between sources, so treat them as a rough guide only.

The names have their own stories. Purgatory is said to come from an American logging supervisor of the Benguet Consolidated mining company in the American colonial period, who struggled here and remarked that it felt like being in purgatory. Mt. Pack is said to be named after William Pack, the governor of Benguet in 1901. These origins come from blog accounts, though, and are not confirmed facts. The charm of this traverse is that it is far less crowded than Pulag and that the scenery keeps changing. You walk through pine forest and trails early on, thick mossy forest in the middle, and open ridges and rural villages later. In clear weather you can see the Benguet mountains and a sea of clouds from the ridge, and one trip report says the Ambangeg trail to Mt. Pulag was visible from the Komkompol side.

It is not an easy mountain, however. It is generally rated 6 out of 9, a major climb, and as a day hike it takes 10 to 12 hours or more. Water is not continuous and injuries are common on the rough road in the final stretch, so allow plenty of stamina and time. If this is your first mountain of this kind, warm up on easier peaks around Baguio first.

blocks.title: From pine forest to mossy forest

children.text: For about the first
5km

after Japas the trail runs through pine forest and mountain paths, then turns to mossy forest as you climb toward Mt. Pack. How much the forest changes within a single route is its biggest attraction.

blocks.title: Mt. Pack and the mossy forest

children.text: Mt. Pack sits on the border of Benguet and Nueva Vizcaya and is listed at about
. You reach it after about
8~9km
from Japas, and after rain the mossy forest glows deep green.

The marker on Mt. Purgatory, which gave the traverse its name, has a toilet and camping space but no water. Trip reports describe it as a cool spot with little sunlight, so fill up plenty of water at Mt. Pack.

Bakian is known to have water and a toilet and is the standard overnight stop on a 2-day, 1-night schedule, while Tangbao has a bunker-style shelter. Some groups have slept in sleeping bags on the Bakian elementary school grounds, so settle the overnight spot with your guide.
Mt. Komkompol, the highest point of the route, is about
. You climb it on the morning of day two and can see the ridge toward Mt. Pulag and a sea of clouds. Some day-hike packages skip it.
About 20 local guides work in this area, and the traverse is an important source of their livelihood. Walking with a guide, you naturally hear about water points, trail forks and village stories.
Some guides describe the hike as looking over Ambuklao Dam and its fish farms. Some travelers combine the traverse with a visit to Ambuklao Dam in the same area.

items.title: Standard 2-day, 1-night schedule
items.subtitle: Walking from Japas to Ekip in two days

children.text: Leave Manila on an overnight bus or a chartered van and travel to Baguio. From Baguio to the trailhead takes about
3 hours
Arrive at the Japas (Bobok-Bisal, Bokod) trailhead, register, and take about
30 minutes
of orientation and guide assignment. Some places also check your blood pressure.
Start trekking. Pass through pine forest and trails, and take your first rest at the Mangangew marker.
Have lunch near Mt. Pack and refill your water. After that you enter the mossy forest.
Reach the Mt. Purgatory marker. Take photos and rest, but move on to the next section before the weather turns.
Arrive at the Bakian or Tangbao shelter and camp. Have dinner and rest early. The temperature drops a lot at night.
Climb Mt. Komkompol for the sunrise and ridge views. After breakfast, pack up and head down.
Arrive near Ekip village or Bokod municipal hall and disperse. The last stretch is a rough road, so stay alert.
The times are a rough flow taken from trip reports. The actual start time and overnight spot depend on the weather and your guide's judgment that day.

items.title: Day traverse
items.subtitle: An early-start schedule for strong hikers

children.text: Arrive at the trailhead, register and attend the briefing. Booking a monster jeep (4×4) in advance for the early morning is common.
Start trekking. Mt. Pack takes about
3~4 hours
, and you reach Mt. Purgatory around noon.
Reaching Mt. Komkompol around this time is typical. After that it takes about
3~5 hours
to descend to Ekip.
Arrive at Ekip around sunset. A headlamp is essential.
The day traverse is physically demanding and has had many accidents. If it is your first time, we recommend the 2-day, 1-night schedule.
Take a bus to Baguio (for example Victory Liner) from the Cubao or Pasay terminal. The trip takes about
6~7 hours
one way, and fares are reported at about
By car, take NLEX, SCTEX and TPLEX, then enter Baguio via Marcos Highway or Kennon Road.
Fares and schedules change from season to season. Check the latest announcements.
Japas is about
60km
from Baguio, and a chartered jeepney or van takes about
2.5~3 hours
The driver's fee depends on group size, and trip reports give a range of
. Your guide or the Bokod tourism office may also recommend a vehicle.
By public transport, you can take a Nueva Vizcaya-bound bus from Baguio via Ambuklao, get off near Bokod municipal hall, and take a motorcycle.

Several mountaineering groups run packages that include assembly in Manila, van transfers, registration, a guide, an environmental donation and meals. In a 2024 report the 2-day, 1-night package cost about
, and day packages are listed at lower prices.

The best time to walk is the dry season from November to April. Views are clearer and the trail is less muddy, so December to March is especially recommended. Even then the mossy forest is damp, and early morning and night temperatures can fall to single digits.

In the rainy season from June to November, leeches are common in the mossy forest, and the trail turns to mud that adds hours to the schedule. If a typhoon approaches, the local government may restrict entry, so check before you leave.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Clear and cool, very cold at night
Most popular season, warm clothing essential
Can be hot by day and water becomes scarcer
Leeches, mud and possible entry restrictions; not recommended for beginners

On the mountain you stay at the Bakian elementary school grounds, the Tangbao shelter or the village of Mangisi. You must bring your own tent or sleeping bag, mat and a thick jacket. Some facilities exist, but do not expect a shower.

The usual approach is to carry your own packed meals and trail food. Some reports say you can order packed meals through your guide. Lodging and restaurants before and after the hike are easiest to find in Baguio city.

Bring a waterproof jacket, warm clothing, a headlamp, personal medicine, a trash bag, trail food and a water bottle of at least 2 liters. For 2 days and 1 night, add a sleeping bag, cooking gear, gloves, a mat and an emergency blanket. Pack as light as you can, and consider a porter if the load is heavy. Carry all your trash back out.
Entry requires advance reservation and a guide. Apply in advance with the Bokod tourism office's form and do not rely on walk-in registration.
Water is not continuous, so refill 2 to 3 liters at every confirmed water point. There is no water at the Purgatory marker.
Trekking poles greatly reduce the strain on your knees on the rough road at the end.
In the rainy season bring leech socks, waterproof gloves and spare socks.
Start walking before 6 to 7 a.m. so you can finish before dark.
The trailhead and the exit are different places, so a vehicle must pick you up again. Book a ride from Ekip to Baguio in advance.
Mobile signal is inconsistent, so bring an offline map and a power bank.
Villages along the way have a custom of leaving a small donation at places such as the elementary school, so follow local guidance.
Once you are on the route it is hard to leave midway. If you feel unwell, talk to your guide early on and turn back.
Greet your guide and the villagers, and ask before taking photos.
Water is scarce, injuries are common on the rough road at the end, and there is a risk of lightning and hypothermia on the ridge, so shorten the plan if the weather turns bad.
A guide is mandatory. Do not go alone or separate from your guide at forks. There are records of people getting lost near Tangbao.
The edges of cliffs in the mossy forest are dangerous even where wooden barriers stand, so walk carefully.
In afternoon fog visibility drops sharply and the temperature falls. Make sure you reach your overnight spot before dark.
Fees, application methods and entry restrictions change often. Check the latest announcements from the Bokod tourism office before you leave.
Distances, elevations and fees differ by source. All figures in this guide are approximate.
The highest mountain on Luzon lies to the north. It is a separate trip that needs a permit and a guide.
In Kabayan village toward Mt. Pulag there are traditional Ibaloi mummy caves.
The hub for lodging, meals and transport before and after the hike. It is about
2.5~3 hours
from the trailhead.
